Mr. Subrata Saha with Mr. Md. Belayet Hossain ------- for the Accused-petitioner.
Mr. A.K.M. Fazlul Haque ------ for the Opposite party No. 2
Mr. Md. Jahangir Alam, Assistant Attorney-General ------ For the Opposite party No. 1
parties:
Md. Rezaul Kabir
Vs.
The State and Another
full_judgment:
Afzal Hossain Ahmed, J: This Rule, at the instance of the accused Md. Rezaul Kabir, was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the proceedings of the Special Case No. 01 of 2009 arising out of Bhaluka Police Station Case No. 25 dated 18.7.2007 under Section 161 of the Penal Code read with Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, now pending in the Court of Special Judge and Sessions Judge, Mymensingh should not be quashed and/or passed such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. One Ruhul Quddus Khan, S.I. of Police, Bhaluka Model Police Station lodged an F.I.R. on 18.7.2007 at about 15-35 hours alleging that he along with his companion forces recovered from the possession of one Md. Rezaul Kabir, Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Bhaluka, Mymensingh an envelope of Khaki colour containing 99 pieces of 500 Taka notes amounting to Tk.49,500/-, each note bearing "M" mark within a round circle mark. While the said accused was receiving the same, as bribe, the Joint Forces at once caught hold of him red-handed and seized the said notes in presence of the witnesses (1) Md. Mosharraf Hossain, A/P Megha Fisheries Ltd. , Bhaluka , Mymensingh, (2) Naik/47910( BDR) Md. Mojibul Haque and (3) Abdur Rashid Fakir. As mentioned in the F.I.R. the aforesaid witness No.1 Md. Mosaharaf Hossain had a dispute over his Megha Fisheries Ltd., now pending in the Land Ministry for settlement, for which the said Upazila Nirbahi Officer demanded Tk.4,00,000/- of which he already paid Tk.10.000/- to the said Upazila Nirbahi Officer. For making payment of the aforesaid Tk. 49,500/- on 18.7.2007 at 12-35 p.m. to the accused the said witness Md. Mosharraf Hossain informed the matter to the Joint Forces upon which the Joint Forces laid trap for catching hold of the said Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Md. Rezaul Kabir red-handed and, accordingly, caught hold of him red handed while he was taking the said amount of money, as bribe, from the witness No.1 Md. Mosharraf Hossain. The Joint Forces also recovered another amount of Tk.15,500/- from the possession of the said Upazila Nirbahi Officer on searching his body for which he could not give any satisfactory answer. The said Upazila Nirbahi Officer being a high Government Official received the said amount of money, as bribe, and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 161 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. The Joint Forces, on search, also recovered two Air Coolers each having 11⁄2 tones capacity which the said Upazila Nirbahi Officer set in his Office by illegal means which the Joint Forces also seized in presence of the witnesses by preparing seizure list. Thereafter, the informant brought the accused along with the seized articles to the aforesaid Police Station and lodged an F.I.R. therewith upon which Bhaluka Model Police Station Case No. 25 dated 18.7.2007 was started. 

 4. Thereafter, one Md. Mojahar Ali Sarder of the Anti-Corruption Commission, Combined District Office, Mymensingh investigated the case and after obtaining sanction from the Commissioner (Investigation) of the Anti-Corruption Commission, Dhaka submitted Charge Sheet' being Charge Sheet No. 328 dated 31.12.2008 under Section 161 of the Penal Code read with Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 against the said accused. 

 5. On 28.01.2009, an application under Section 265C of the Code of Criminal Procedure was filed before the learned Special Judge and Session Judge, Mymensingh, on behalf of the accused-petitioner, wherein he claimed himself absolutely innocent and also claimed that in this case he has been made a victim of a deep rooted conspiracy and that the instant case being a trap case the mandatory provisions of law prescribed therefore, in laying and conducting a trap case has not, at all, been followed and as such the case is not maintainable and the accused is entitled to be discharged. 

 8. Mr. Subrata Saha, with Mr. Md. Belayet Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the accused-petitioner submits that the accused-petitioner is absolutely innocent and he has been made a victim of a deep rooted conspiracy over a dispute concerning Megha Fisheries Ltd. against whom the accused-petitioner submitted reports to the Land Ministry thrice and that on the basis of those reports Bhaluka Police Station Case No. 34 dated 18.6.2007 was started against the said Megha Fisheries Ltd. Thereafter, one Mosharraf Hossain of the said Megha Fisheries Ltd. made the conspiracy and hatched up this case against the accused-petitioner making him a victim of the conspiracy. However, the case, as initiated, is apparently a trap case for initiation of which special procedure has been laid down in the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007, the alleged offence being included in the schedule to the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004. Mr. Saha further submits that the provisions of Rule 16(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 are mandatory provisions to be followed in laying and conducting the trap cases but that has not, at all, been complied with in the instant case. Thus, the very initiation of the instant proceedings being illegal are liable to be quashed. 

 10. Mr. A.K.M. Fazlul Hoque, the learned Advocate appearing for the Anti-Corruption Commission submits that the accused-petitioner was caught red handed in a trap case conducted by the Joint Forces on 18.7.2007 when the Emergency Power Ordinance, 2007 and Emergency Power Rules, 2007 had been in force and that the law enforcing agencies, under the Emergency Power Rules, 14 and 15, with a view to prevent corruption, were vested with the power to arrest, inquire and investigate such cases. He further submits that there is no infirmity of law in launching the instant prosecution against the accused-petitioner and as such the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 12. The point calls for determination in this case is whether the instant proceeding is liable to be quashed as prayed for by the accused-petitioner. 

 14. The offence under Section 161 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 has been included in the schedule to the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004. Under the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 the trap cases have been distinguished from all other corruption cases and for laying and conducting trap cases some special procedure has been laid down in Rule 16(1) (now so to say Rule 16 since Rule 16(2) has been omitted, vide S.R.O. No. 265-Ain/2007 dated 26.11.2007) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007. The amended Rule 16 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules  2007 reads as follows:- 

 ১৬। ফাঁদ মামলা (Trap case) দূর্নীতি প্রতিরোধের নিমিক্তে আইনের তফসিলভুক্ত অপরাধে জড়িত কোন ব্যক্তি বা ব্যক্তিবর্গকে হাতে নাতে ধৃত করিবার উদ্দেশ্য তদন্তের দায়িত্ব প্রাপ্ত কমিশনার এর অনুমোদনক্রমে তৎকর্তৃক ক্ষমতাপ্রাপ্ত কর্মকর্তা ফাঁদ মামলা (Trap case) প্রস্তুত করিতে বা পরিচালনা করিতে পারিবেন। 

 15. The trap cases have been distinguished from all other corruption cases and the offence under Section 161 of the Penal Code read with Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 being included in the schedule to the Anti-Corruption Commission Act. 2004 all the trap cases are required to be conducted as provided under Rule 16 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007. 

 16. Rule 16 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 requires that with a view to preventing corruption, Officer empowered by the Commissioner in-charge, for the purpose to catch hold of any person or persons red handed connected with the offences specified in the schedule to the Act, may subject to the approval of the Commissioner-in-charge, lay the trap and conduct the trap operation but, admittedly, the said provisions of law have not, at all, been followed in laying and conducting the trap in the instant case. 

 17. Mr. A.K.M. Fazlul Hoque, the learned Advocate appearing for the Anti-Corruption Commission has submitted that the alleged offence took place during the period when Emergency power Ordinance, 2007 and Emergency power Rules, 2007 had been in force and that under Rule 15 of the Emergency Power Rules, 2007 the Joint Forces as well the law enforcing agencies were empowered to inquire, investigate and arrest any person with a view to preventing corruption or other offences mentioned in Rules 14 and 15 thereof and that since the accused-petitioner was arrested by the Joint Forces and the case was initiated at their instance, the Rule 16 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 was not applicable to this case at the time and, thus, the initiation of the instant case suffers from no infirmity of law. 

 19. From the recital of Rule 12 of the Special Power Rules, 2007, as referred to above, it is apparent that for the purpose of lodging complaint, furnishing first information, inquiry into all other pretrial proceedings, trial and appeal shall be done or to be disposed of under the said Special Power Rules, 2007 and the Code of Criminal Procedure and when there is special laws for the offences mentioned in the said Special Power Rules such special laws shall be followed for the purposes mentioned as above. In view thereof the offence as alleged in the instant case since relates to a trap case within the meaning of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 and these being the special laws, Rule 16 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 was required to have been followed in initiating a trap case which precisely has not, at all, been followed in the instant case, being a trap case. 

 21. The above Rules 14 and 15 of the Emergency Power Rules, 2007 also do not absolve the members of the Joint Forces and law enforcing agencies from complying with the provisions as laid down in Rule 16 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 in laying and conducting the trap cases. 

 24. But when the public duty is imposed and the statute requires that something shall be performed in a certain manner or under some specified conditions, such prescriptions may well be regarded as intended to be mandatory in cases where those exercising the duty were obliged to fulfill such essential and imperative requirements of law, such requirements of law if not fulfilled would cause injustice to the accused. 

 25. In view of the above, as contemplated in Rule 16 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007, as referred to above, we find that the legislature or the framers of the law expressed their intention that in laying and conducting a trap case to catch hold of a public servant red handed connected with the offence as mentioned in the schedule to the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 the provisions laid down in Rule 16 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 shall be followed. There is no scope on the part of the Court to put a different word to give a different meaning other than the one which was meant by the expression employed by the framers of the law. Therefore, the provisions as laid down in Rule 16 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 are construed to be mandatory. 

 26. Mr. Subrata Saha, the learned Advocate appearing for the accused-petitioner, in appreciation of his submission, has cited a decision in the case of Abdur Rashid Vs. the State reported in 60 D.L.R. (HCD)(2008)629 wherein it has been held as under:- 

 "10.- Arrest of Government servant in an anti-corruption drive to catch hold any person or persons red-handed connected with the offence by any police officer not duly empowered by the Commission or the Commissioner in charge of the commission in laying the trap and conducting the trap operation by abusing official power is wild goose chase which by itself tantamounts to corruption therefore, and such exercise by police officer not empowered by the Commission as has been done in the instant case is, prima facie, malafide and repressive and liable to be struck down and accused petitioner unlawfully arrested and detained is liable to be released on bail despite bar to seek bail under Rule 19 (Gha) of the Emergency Power Rules, 2007. 

 27. It appears that the aforesaid observations in 60 D.L.R. (2008) (HCD) 629 were made as 'obiter dictum' in a Criminal Miscellaneous Case for bail under Section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure arising out of a case under Section 161 of the Penal Code read with Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and Rule 19(Gha) of the Emergency Power Rules, 2007. However, upon consideration of the facts, the case being a trap case, the mandatory provisions of Rule 16(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission, Rules, 2007 in lying and conducting the trap, similar to that of the instant case, having not been followed the very arrest of the accused and initiation of the proceeding against him, being illegal, the Court released the accused-petitioner on bail despite of bar to seek bail under Rule 19(gha) of the Emergency Power Rules, 2007 at that time. 

 29. Keeping that view in mind, in administering justice, a duty is also cast upon the Court to see whether the imperative provisions of law as intended and meant by the legislature or the framers of law has been duly complied with in launching the prosecution against a person and having not so complied with there might be every likelihood of causing miscarriage of justice and unnecessary victimization of the accused to suit one's own purpose or jealousy as has been focused in the instant case on behalf of the accused-petitioner. 

 30. Considering all the above aspects of the matter we find that in laying and conducting the trap in the instant case, as alleged, the mandatory provisions of Rule 16 of the Anti-Corruption Rules, 2007 were not, at all, followed which vitiates the very initiation of the proceedings in question. Thus, the institution and continuation of the instant proceedings amounts to an abuse of the process of the Court which is liable to be quashed. We find merit in this Rule. 

 32. The proceedings of the Special Case No. 01 of 2009 arising out of Bhaluka Model Police Station Case No. 25 dated 18.7.2007 under section 161 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 now pending in the Court of Special Judge and Sessions Judge, Mymensingh are quashed.
